assumptions.text: The language is Rust. The ticket of this step states it, README.md names it, and every existing crate is Rust. The framework is none: plain Rust with rusqlite for the ledger, as horch-core uses today.

Each context is 1 module under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain/, application/ and adapters/ submodules (decision D1, understand N6). Existing modules (taskledger, vcs, runtime, roster, harness, routing, workspace) are wrapped by adapters and are not moved in this plan.

Attempt and its Lease are entities and value objects inside the Task aggregate, not their own aggregate (decision D2), because 04 S7 needs the end of the attempt and the requeue of the task in 1 ledger transaction.

Only the verification module can construct a VerifiedVerdict value, and Task::mark_done takes one; the one-door transition table also refuses verifying -> done with any cause other than verifier (decision D4, define N1).

Concurrency inside the ledger needs no optimistic retry: fleetd is the single writer and runs its pass serially (connect D1, design Ledger). Each aggregate still carries a version, and the one-door transition checks from_state, so a stale write fails loudly.
The attempts table holds task attempts (written by task-execution) and sub-orchestrator attempts with task_id null (written by ideas). Each context writes only its own row kind (organise N2).

The platform layer lives at crates/horch-core/src/platform/ with mod.rs (the trait and NotSupported) and mac.rs, linux.rs, windows.rs; it is owned by fleet-runtime (design D1, strategize N1). Only these 3 files hold cfg(target_os).

The implementation plan follows the 8 phases of the design migration plan in order (Phase 0 to Phase 7). Slice numbers follow the phases, so a slice is released only when its fault-injection gate passes (design D9).
The fitness tests extend crates/horch-core/tests/arch_scan.rs, which already scans source files for forbidden lines. No new tool is needed.
Coined terms Verified Verdict, Stall Rung, Judged Tree, Path Claim, Awake Instant and Judge Finding name value objects and an entity that the canvases describe but do not name.

open_questions.text: Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper logic (connect D2, still open)? This step recommends fleet-runtime and keeps the composition root at crates/horch/src/cmd/fleet_run.rs in every option, so slices 0 to 3 do not depend on the answer. Slice 4 (Phase 4) needs it.

Must the arch_scan fitness test also enforce that no context reads or writes the tables or folders of another context (organise Q2)? This step plans the rule as fitness_no_context_touches_foreign_tables and recommends yes.

Docs sync and adapter conformance have no owning context (organise D2 open). This step places run-conformance-tests in worker-profiles and leaves docs sync out of the plan until organise D2 is answered.

herdr agent status is a liveness signal of task-execution with no connect message (define Q2). This step reads it through the LivenessProbe port over the fleet-runtime HerdrGateway. Must ddd-connect add the message?

Does a feature rebase wait for the running attempts of the feature, or do their task branches rebase at landing (define Q3)? This step models the second: a task branch that no longer applies goes to conflicted at build-bundle.
Migration of the 178 existing OS-specific sites into the platform layer is a separate decision (design D1). This plan touches only new fleetd code and the adapters that wrap existing modules.

coined_terms.definition: The value that only the verification module can create, and the only input that moves a task to done.
1 step of the stall ladder: first doorbell, second doorbell, or end of the attempt.
A time reading that counts only awake machine time, used for leases and stall rungs.
The set of paths a running task owns; 2 running tasks of 1 feature never hold overlapping claims.
1 miss that a judge task reports, with a rank of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.
The tree hash that a check, a review or a gate judged; a pass stands only while the tree is the same.

domain_services.name: PlanValidator

application_services.name: AddIdea
application_services.description: horch idea add "..." or -f notes.md, optional --to <feature>.

application_services.name: StartSubOrchestrator
application_services.description: fleetd starts 1 fresh process per phase in the pane of the feature, and restarts a dead or missing one on the next pass. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after commit (connect N3).

application_services.name: AskOperator
application_services.description: 1 question at a time: what done looks like, scope edges, constraints, affected areas, priority.

application_services.name: AnswerInterviewQuestion
application_services.description: The operator answers in the pane. horch idea note records it.

application_services.name: AmendIdea
application_services.description: horch idea amend <id> "...".

application_services.name: WriteAssumptions
application_services.description: Writes assumptions.md: [confirmed] and [assumed] items, none [open].

application_services.name: RequestApproval
application_services.description: Moves the idea to awaiting_approval and notifies the operator. Reminds once an hour in working hours.

application_services.name: ParkIdea
application_services.description: Issued by policy after 7 days of waiting or an escalation. The operator also runs horch idea park.

application_services.name: CancelIdea
application_services.description: horch idea cancel.

application_services.name: ReviseAssumptions
application_services.description: horch idea revise <id> "...".

application_services.name: ApproveAssumptions
application_services.description: horch idea approve <id>. Refused inside any fleet attempt; profiles deny it. fleetd writes approval.json with the sha256 the operator saw; any other approval file is ignored (I7).

application_services.name: AddDirectIdea
application_services.description: horch idea add --direct <ticket file>, optional --to. Refused inside a fleet attempt.

application_services.name: WriteSpec
application_services.description: Writes spec.md and requirements.yaml after approval.

application_services.name: SubmitPlan
application_services.description: Writes tickets and plan.yaml.

application_services.name: ValidatePlan
application_services.description: The plan validator: paired judges, declared gates, model guide, overlapping paths. Commits tasks in 1 transaction.

application_services.name: AskQuestion
application_services.description: Writes 1 question file, commits work in progress, exits.

application_services.name: AnswerQuestion
application_services.description: fleetd starts the owner on each pass until an answer is recorded. 4 cases (design, Ideas, How a worker's question is resolved).

application_services.name: EscalateQuestion
application_services.description: Fires when the time limit of the question row passes.

application_services.name: ReplanTask
application_services.description: Once per task.

application_services.name: RollUpIdea
application_services.description: in_progress to integrating.

application_services.name: CloseIdea
application_services.description: Needs every worktree of the idea removed.

aggregates.name: Task
invariants: I1: a leased or running task has exactly 1 unexpired lease and 1 live attempt
I2: no task is ready while a dependency is not done
Only a VerifiedVerdict from the verification module moves a task to done (RR-3, define N1)
A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal (04 S7)
A usage limit burns no attempt (RR-11)
An operator requeue resets the attempt count through attempt_floor (04 L8)
A task has at most max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then escalation (RR-6)
state_transitions: pending -> ready (promote-task, every dependency done)
ready -> leased (dispatch-task, lease and worktree row in 1 transaction)
leased -> running (launch-attempt, after worktree-created)
running -> running (renew-lease, earned activity only)
running -> stalled (renew-lease lease-expired, or apply-stall-ladder)
running -> verifying (attempt exit with a result file; write-result alone never leaves verifying)
running -> waiting_quota (move-to-fallback with no fallback on another provider)
running -> leased (move-to-fallback onto a fallback persona; attempt count unchanged)
running -> blocked_on_user (worker question; exec worker exits and the task parks)
waiting_quota -> ready (promote-task on quota-window-reset)
blocked_on_user -> leased (question-answered or own-assumption-recorded)
stalled|verifying -> failed (end-attempt with a non-verified outcome)
failed -> ready (schedule-retry while attempts remain)
failed -> escalated (escalate-task after the replan, or rescue-failed)
verifying -> done (mark-task-done with a VerifiedVerdict only)
escalated -> ready (requeue-task by the operator, attempt_floor reset)
any non-terminal -> cancelled (plan change)
rejected: done from any state without a VerifiedVerdict
rejected: ready while a dependency is not done
rejected: leased for a worker that already runs an attempt (I4)

aggregates.name: Verification
invariants: A verdict is verified only when result.json validates and the check passes in the worker sandbox
A code kind is verified only after the review scripts pass (V-14 limits)
A judgment kind is verified only with no open CRITICAL judge finding
At most 2 critical fix rounds, then the task escalates
A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW finding
state_transitions: pending -> checking (run-check, result.json validates)
checking -> check_failed (run-check, check-failed)
checking -> reviewing (check-passed, code kind)
checking -> awaiting_judge (check-passed, judgment kind)
checking -> verified (check-passed, judge kind: structural check only)
reviewing -> verified (review-passed)
reviewing -> review_failed (review-failed)
awaiting_judge -> verified (write-judge-verdict, no CRITICAL item)
awaiting_judge -> critical_fix (open-critical-fix, round 1 or 2)
critical_fix -> awaiting_judge (fix written, a fresh judge checks the earlier CRITICAL items only)
critical_fix -> escalated (a CRITICAL item left after 2 rounds)
rejected: verified from pending, checking without a passed check, or awaiting_judge with an open CRITICAL item

domain_services.name: DispatchPlanner
domain_services.description: Picks ready tasks for workers across Task instances: I4, path overlap (04 L6), exclusive tasks, health guards and pool pacing. Pure: takes snapshots and a Clock reading.

domain_services.name: StallLadder
domain_services.description: Maps a liveness snapshot (process alive, heartbeat age, activity age, agent state) and an awake-time reading to the next rung: doorbell, doorbell, end.

application_services.name: PromoteTask
application_services.description: pending to ready when every dependency is done, or waiting_quota to ready when the pool resets.

application_services.name: DispatchTask
application_services.description: No cap. Only the health guards (free disk, load) and the pacing of the pool hold dispatch.

application_services.name: LaunchAttempt
application_services.description: Starts the wrapper and the CLI in its own process group. A resume after an answer also launches. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after the ledger transaction commits (connect N3, N4).

application_services.name: RenewLease
application_services.description: Every reconcile pass (5 s). Lease time counts only while the machine is awake.

application_services.name: ApplyStallLadder
application_services.description: Every pass: doorbell, doorbell after 2 min, then end. stall_after default 5 min; start timeout 90 s.

application_services.name: MoveToFallback
application_services.description: Fallback persona on another provider, else waiting_quota with the lease paused.

application_services.name: WriteResult
application_services.description: horch result writes outbox/result.json. Records the result on the Attempt. It never moves the task to done (define N1).

application_services.name: RunCheck
application_services.description: The verifier, with today's check timeout (20 min, max 24 h).

application_services.name: RunReview
application_services.description: Today's review scripts, unchanged. Rounds: light 1, full 3.

application_services.name: WriteJudgeVerdict
application_services.description: The worker of a judge task writes its verdict file.

application_services.name: OpenCriticalFix
application_services.description: At most 2 fix rounds.

application_services.name: SettleHighFinding
application_services.description: Fix or dismiss with a written reason.

application_services.name: EndAttempt
application_services.description: Stops the process group through the platform layer (Linux: SIGINT, 20 s, SIGKILL).

application_services.name: ScheduleRetry
application_services.description: Reads max_attempts and backoff from the profile.

application_services.name: EscalateTask
application_services.description: Writes to needs-you/ and posts a herdr notification.

application_services.name: RequeueTask
application_services.description: Resets attempt_floor.

application_services.name: MarkTaskDone
application_services.description: The verifier writes verdict.json. Takes a VerifiedVerdict; only the verification module can construct one (D4).

aggregates.name: Feature
invariants: I8: a feature is merged only when its changes are in the primary branch by content, also after a squash merge
I9: a feature branch moves only by fast-forward to a candidate that passed its gate
I10: before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists
A feature is ready only with a full gate pass on its current tip over the current primary branch
A gate pass goes stale when either judged tip moves (04 F5)
A feature is stacked on at most 1 older feature
state_transitions: open -> open (rebase-feature-branch, rescue ref first; a conflict opens a resolver task)
open -> open (stack-feature after trial-merge-conflicted)
open -> ready (mark-feature-ready, current full gate pass)
ready -> open (a tip moves; the full gate pass goes stale)
ready -> merged (check-merged finds the changes by content)
open|ready -> abandoned (operator)
rejected: ready without a current full gate pass
rejected: merged read from the GitHub API alone
rejected: rebase with no rescue ref of the old tip

aggregates.name: TaskBranch
invariants: I8: a task branch is landed only when its changes are in the feature branch by content
I11: every fleet branch in git has a branches row; one without is adopted as an orphan row, never deleted
I12: a branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it
A task branch is ready only when its task is done (verified)
Under the land lock, just before the fast-forward, the task is still landing and held by its worker (04 F9)
A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7)
An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator and only after worktree-rescued (connect N4)
state_transitions: building -> verifying (task enters verifying)
verifying -> ready (mark-branch-ready on task-done)
ready -> in_bundle (build-bundle, queue order)
in_bundle -> conflicted (build-bundle, rebase conflict; the task goes back to its worker)
in_bundle -> landed (fast-forward-feature-branch after fast-gate-passed, under the land lock)
in_bundle -> gate_failed (bisect-bundle finds it; open-triage-task)
conflicted -> verifying (a new attempt of the same worker)
gate_failed -> verifying (triage task fixed)
any -> abandoned (abandon-task-branch by the operator, after worktree-rescued)
rejected: ready while the task is not done
rejected: landed for a cancelled task (04 F9)
rejected: deletion without landed, merged or rescued

decisions.question: Where do the 6 context modules live in the existing crates?

options.summary: New modules crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain, application and adapters; existing modules become adapters behind the new ports.
pros: Matches understand N6: contexts are modules inside horch-core
Clear seam for the fitness tests
Existing tests of taskledger and vcs keep running while phases land
cons: 2 code paths exist until each phase retires the old one
Adapters wrap code that is not hexagonal
risks: Old and new paths drift if a phase leaves the old one in place

options.summary: Evolve existing modules in place: taskledger becomes task-execution, vcs becomes integration, and so on.
pros: No wrapper code
1 code path at all times
cons: Existing modules mix concerns of several contexts (taskledger holds worktrees, landing and tasks)
No place for the dependency rule
risks: A large refactor before Phase 1 can start

options.summary: A new crate horch-fleetd that horch depends on.
pros: Compiler-enforced boundary to horch-core
cons: Cyclic needs: fleetd adapters wrap horch-core modules and horch-core tests need fleetd
risks: Build time and a crate split nobody asked for

decisions.rationale: understand N6 puts the contexts inside horch-core, and the migration plan replaces old behaviour phase by phase, so the old modules must keep working behind adapters until their phase retires them.
would_flip_if: The operator wants a crate boundary enforced by the compiler
A phase retires a whole existing module at once, so wrapping it costs more than moving it

decisions.question: Is Attempt its own aggregate or an entity inside Task?

options.summary: 3 aggregates as discover proposes: Task, Attempt, Verification.
pros: Small aggregates
Attempt rows of sub-orchestrators fit without a task
cons: 04 S7 needs the attempt end and the task requeue in 1 transaction, which crosses 2 aggregates
risks: A crash between the 2 writes loses the requeue (the #216 bug)

options.summary: Task holds its Attempts and the Lease; Verification stays its own aggregate.
pros: 04 S7 and I1 are 1-aggregate transactions
A task has at most max_attempts attempts, so the aggregate stays small
Verification runs long checks outside the task transaction
cons: Sub-orchestrator attempts (task_id null) are not part of this aggregate and are written by ideas
risks: Task grows if attempts keep transcripts; they must keep only ids and outcomes

options.summary: 1 Task aggregate that also holds the verification state.
pros: 1 aggregate for every task fact
cons: A 20 min check holds the task aggregate
The only-the-verifier-sets-done rule has no module seam
risks: define N1 is harder to prove

decisions.rationale: 04 S7 is a preservation row: the reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal. With 1 aggregate per transaction, the attempt must be inside Task. Verification stays apart so the verifier is the only module that can produce a VerifiedVerdict (define N1).
would_flip_if: The ledger allows a multi-aggregate transaction as an explicit exception for the reap
Attempts must carry large state such as transcripts

decisions.question: Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper logic (connect D2)?

options.summary: task-execution: the wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, which are task-execution facts.
pros: The files it writes feed the lease and the stall ladder
cons: task-execution would start processes, against connect N3
risks: The process-group and sandbox code leaks into a core context

options.summary: worker-profiles: the wrapper builds the private config home and maps CLI events per adapter.
pros: Per-CLI event mapping sits with the harness adapters
cons: worker-profiles would own a process role and the 256k context guard at run time

options.summary: fleet-runtime: the wrapper is a process role of the binary, like fleetd and fleetd check; it asks worker-profiles for the CLI event map.
pros: Process groups, the platform layer and atomic file writes already live there
Keeps both core contexts free of process code
cons: fleet-runtime is already the largest supporting context
risks: The CLI event map crosses from worker-profiles at run time

decisions.rationale: Recommended option C. Strongest argument against it: fleet-runtime then owns 4 process roles and the team has high cognitive load (organise warning). The call is upstream (connect D2) and stays open for the operator.
would_flip_if: The operator assigns the wrapper in connect D2
The CLI event map turns out to need task state

decisions.question: How does the code make the verification module the only writer of done (define N1)?

options.summary: A VerifiedVerdict type with a constructor private to the verification module; Task::mark_done takes it.
pros: The compiler refuses any other path
cons: A type alone does not stop a raw SQL update
risks: A test helper exposes the constructor

options.summary: The one-door transition table refuses verifying -> done unless the cause is verifier.
pros: Holds for every writer of the ledger
risks: Any caller can pass the cause string

options.summary: Both A and B, plus the test fm_result_file_alone_leaves_task_verifying.
pros: Compile-time and run-time guards
The design already requires the one-door table

decisions.rationale: The design requires the one-door transition table, so B costs nothing extra; A adds a compile-time guard for in-process callers, and define N1 asks for a test.
would_flip_if: The one-door table is dropped from the design

notes_for_downstream.text: The code step adds no message across a process boundary. start-agent-process and launch-environment stay in-process calls (ports AgentProcesses and LaunchEnvironmentQuery). The file protocol (result.json, exit.json, heartbeat.json, idea-folder files) and the command channel are the contracts that need schemas.

Each contract test name in code.json is 'contract: <message id>' and each idempotency test is 'idempotent: <message id>'. ddd-contracts should use the connect payloads of these messages and the idempotency keys as written.

plain_words.what: This step turns the 6 parts of the fleetd design into a code plan for Rust: which folders, which types, which interfaces, which tests, and in which order to build them. It writes no code.
plain_words.decided: All 6 parts live as modules under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/. Only the 2 core parts get aggregates (rich objects that guard their own rules): Task and Verification in task-execution, Feature and TaskBranch in integration. An attempt lives inside its task, so a crash can never end the attempt and forget the task. 140 named tests cover the 13 invariants, the preservation rows and 10 high-priority fault scenarios. The build order is the 8 phases of the design.
plain_words.assumed: We assumed the existing modules stay where they are and get wrapped, not moved. We also assumed nothing else may mark a task done: only the verifier can create the value that does it.
plain_words.riskiest: Wrapping old modules means 2 code paths live side by side until each phase removes the old one. If a phase forgets to remove its old path, the old watchdog and the new fleetd can both act on 1 task. The owner of the per-attempt wrapper program is still open and must be chosen before Phase 4.
